questions.prompt: Which argument proves the identity (x² + y²)² = (x² - y²)² + (2xy)²?
questions.prompt_markup: Which argument proves the identity (x² + y²)² = (x² - y²)² + (2xy)²?

choices.text: For x = 2 and y = 1: 25 = 9 + 16, so the identity is true.
Take the square root of both sides: x² + y² = (x² - y²) + 2xy, and the right side simplifies to x² - y² + 2xy, so the identity is true.
The left side is x⁴ + 2x²y² + y⁴. The right side is x⁴ - 2x²y² + y⁴ + 4x²y² = x⁴ + 2x²y² + y⁴. The sides are equal.
The right side is (x² - y²)² + (2xy)² = x⁴ - y⁴ + 4x²y², and the left side is x⁴ + y⁴ + 4x²y², so the two sides are equal.

questions.correct_answer: The left side is x⁴ + 2x²y² + y⁴. The right side is x⁴ - 2x²y² + y⁴ + 4x²y² = x⁴ + 2x²y² + y⁴. The sides are equal.
questions.grading_note: Both sides expand to x⁴ + 2x²y² + y⁴. The others check one example, square x² - y² as x⁴ - y⁴, or take square roots term by term.

questions.prompt: Which argument proves the identity a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²)?
questions.prompt_markup: Which argument proves the identity a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²)?

choices.text: The product is a³ - a²b + ab² + a²b - ab² + b³. The terms -a²b and a²b cancel, ab² and -ab² cancel, leaving a³ + b³.
For a = 1 and b = 2 the left side is 1 + 8 = 9 and the right side is 3 · (1 - 2 + 4) = 9, so the identity is true for all a and b.
Multiply the first terms and the last terms: a · a² = a³ and b · b² = b³, so the product is a³ + b³.
The product is a³ - 2a²b + b³, which equals a³ + b³.

questions.correct_answer: The product is a³ - a²b + ab² + a²b - ab² + b³. The terms -a²b and a²b cancel, ab² and -ab² cancel, leaving a³ + b³.
questions.grading_note: All six products, then the cancellations. The others check one example, skip four of the six products, or multiply incorrectly.

questions.prompt: Which argument proves the identity (a + b)² - (a - b)² = 4ab?
questions.prompt_markup: Which argument proves the identity (a + b)² - (a - b)² = 4ab?

choices.text: For a = 3 and b = 1: 16 - 4 = 12 = 4 · 3, so the identity is true.
(a² + 2ab + b²) - (a² - 2ab + b²) = a² + 2ab + b² - a² + 2ab - b² = 4ab.
(a + b)² - (a - b)² = (a² + b²) - (a² - b²) = a² + b² - a² + b² = 4ab.

questions.correct_answer: (a² + 2ab + b²) - (a² - 2ab + b²) = a² + 2ab + b² - a² + 2ab - b² = 4ab.
questions.grading_note: Subtract the whole second square, changing the sign of every term (or factor as [(a + b) - (a - b)][(a + b) + (a - b)] = (2b)(2a)). The others check one example, square binomials as a² + b², or use the false rule x² - y² = (x - y)².

questions.prompt: Which argument proves the identity x⁴ + 4 = (x² + 2x + 2)(x² - 2x + 2)?
questions.prompt_markup: Which argument proves the identity x⁴ + 4 = (x² + 2x + 2)(x² - 2x + 2)?

choices.text: The right side is ((x² + 2) + 2x)((x² + 2) - 2x) = (x² + 2)² + (2x)² = x⁴ + 4x² + 4 - 4x² = x⁴ + 4.
For x = 0: 4 = 2 · 2, so the identity is true.
The right side is ((x² + 2) + 2x)((x² + 2) - 2x) = (x² + 2)² - (2x)² = x⁴ + 4x² + 4 - 4x² = x⁴ + 4.
Multiply the first terms and the last terms: x² · x² = x⁴ and 2 · 2 = 4.

questions.correct_answer: The right side is ((x² + 2) + 2x)((x² + 2) - 2x) = (x² + 2)² - (2x)² = x⁴ + 4x² + 4 - 4x² = x⁴ + 4.
questions.grading_note: Group as a difference of squares (or expand all nine products). The others check one example, use (u + v)(u - v) = u² + v², or skip the middle products.

Yes: a fourth power applies to each term inside the parentheses, so (a - b)⁴ = a⁴ - b⁴ for all a and b.

questions.domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions
questions.skill: Prove identities with the Binomial Theorem
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Which argument uses the Binomial Theorem to prove that the entries in row n of Pascal's Triangle add to 2ⁿ?
questions.prompt_markup: Which argument uses the Binomial Theorem to prove that the entries in row n of Pascal's Triangle add to 2ⁿ?

choices.text: Row n has n + 1 entries, and each entry is the sum of the two entries above it, so every row has twice as many entries as the row before it and the sum of row n is 2ⁿ.
Row 3 is 1, 3, 3, 1, which adds to 8 = 2³, so every row n adds to 2ⁿ.
Set x = y = 1 in (x + y)ⁿ = C(n, 0)xⁿ + C(n, 1)xⁿ⁻¹y + ... + C(n, n)yⁿ. The left side is 2ⁿ and the right side is C(n, 0) + C(n, 1) + ... + C(n, n), the row sum.
Set x = 1 and y = 0 in (x + y)ⁿ = C(n, 0)xⁿ + ... + C(n, n)yⁿ: the left side is 1 and the right side is C(n, 0) = 1, so each row adds to 2ⁿ.

questions.correct_answer: Set x = y = 1 in (x + y)ⁿ = C(n, 0)xⁿ + C(n, 1)xⁿ⁻¹y + ... + C(n, n)yⁿ. The left side is 2ⁿ and the right side is C(n, 0) + C(n, 1) + ... + C(n, n), the row sum.
questions.grading_note: Substituting 1 for x and y makes every term equal to its coefficient. The others check one row, use a substitution that gives 1, or argue from the number of entries.
